chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Uramah, from one who narrated to him, from Ali ibn Maymun al-Sa'igh, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
O Ali! Visit Husayn and do not neglect it.
I asked, "What is the reward for one who goes to him?"
He said: "Whoever goes to him on foot, Allah will record for him one good deed for every step, erase one bad deed, and raise his rank."
When he arrives, Allah will assign two angels to him who will write whatever good comes out of his mouth, and they will not write whatever bad comes out of his mouth or anything else.
When he departs, they will bid him farewell and say, "O friend of Allah! You are forgiven. You are from the party of Allah, the party of His Messenger, and the party of the family of His Messenger."
And by Allah, you will never see Hell with your own eyes, nor will it see you, nor burn you forever.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific rewards and spiritual benefits of visiting Imam Husayn (a.s.) on foot according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) highlighting the unique spiritual economy of Ziyarah, where physical effort is transmuted into divine merit. The specific detail of angels recording only the good spoken by the visitor underscores the concept of *al-Hasanah al-Khassah* (special good deeds) granted to the pilgrim, reinforcing the Shia belief in the intercessory and purifying power of visiting the Imams. This promise of deliverance from Hellfire connects the act of visitation directly to the ultimate eschatological hope of the Ahl al-Bayt's followers.
